alabama.delivery: The Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles (ABPP), a state agency, supervises both probation and parole. Its field offices and probation and parole officers handle people the circuit courts place on probation across Alabama.
alabama.violations: ABPP's official probation brochure says that if an officer has a good and valid reason to think a condition of probation was broken, a report of violation is filed with the sentencing court and the District Attorney. The court then holds a probation violation hearing (the brochure says within 30 days); the person can speak about the violation and present evidence, and the judge can revoke probation and impose the sentence, keep the person on probation with the same conditions, or add conditions such as jail time, more drug testing, or community service.
alabama.early: Alabama's probation statute (Ala. Code section 15-22-54(d), quoted in ABPP materials) says the court may discharge a probationer early and end the probation period 'at or after two years,' and the agency brochure says at the end of probation the officer submits a request to the judge to end supervision, with early termination possible in some cases.
alabama.fees: ABPP states that people on supervision pay a monthly supervision fee set by Alabama law (Ala. Code section 15-22-2) of $40 per month, plus any court costs, fines, and restitution the court orders.
alabama.link_label: Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles (paroles.alabama.gov)

alaska.delivery: The Division of Probation and Parole within the Alaska Department of Corrections supervises adult probation statewide. Probation and parole officers in district offices across Alaska supervise people placed on probation by the courts, under the division director and the Commissioner of Corrections.
alaska.violations: Alaska DOC materials describe the violation process as officer reports and disposition work filed with the sentencing court, and petitions to revoke probation are heard by the court under AS 12.55.110. Because no single official DOC or Alaska Court System page lays out the full hearing steps and outcomes in plain terms, only the structure (officer report to the court, court hearing, court decides) can be stated from the official sources opened.
alaska.link_label: Alaska Department of Corrections — Division of Probation and Parole

arizona.delivery: In Arizona, adult probation is run by the courts: each county's Adult Probation Department works for the Superior Court in that county, under the oversight of the Administrative Office of the Courts (Arizona Judicial Branch). There is no state corrections probation agency; probation officers are court employees in all 15 counties.
arizona.violations: Arizona's probation statute (A.R.S. section 13-901(C), quoted on the Arizona courts' pages) says that if there is good cause to think a person has violated probation, the court can issue a summons or warrant, and at a hearing the court may revoke, suspend, or continue probation, or impose added conditions such as jail time, fines, or community service. County court pages (e.g., Yavapai County Superior Court) describe the same process: petition to revoke, initial appearance, and a violation hearing before the sentencing judge.
arizona.fees: Arizona law (A.R.S. section 13-901(A)) requires the court, as a condition of probation, to assess a monthly fee of not less than $65 — unless the court finds the person unable to pay and sets a lower amount.
arizona.link_label: Arizona Judicial Branch — Adult Probation (Administrative Office of the Courts)

arkansas.delivery: In Arkansas, adult probation is supervised by the Division of Community Correction (DCC), part of the Arkansas Department of Corrections. DCC probation and parole officers staff area offices across the state and supervise people placed on probation by the circuit courts.
arkansas.violations: DCC's official 'On Probation' guidance and Arkansas's probation statute (A.C.A. section 16-93-308) describe revocation this way: a violation can lead to a court petition and a revocation hearing, typically within 30 days of arrest; at the hearing the person has the right to an attorney and to present a defense, and the judge may continue or modify probation or revoke it and impose a sentence that could have been imposed before probation was granted.
arkansas.early: Arkansas law (A.C.A. section 16-93-1906, enacted by Act 423 of 2025) provides for early termination reports: a probation and parole officer can certify a person as eligible for early termination after at least one year of compliant supervision, the court holds a hearing, and the judge may end probation early if statutory requirements are met.
arkansas.fees: Arkansas law (A.C.A. section 16-93-104) sets the monthly supervision fee at $35. The Board of Corrections may adjust the fee by rule within limits the statute sets, and an increase may not push it above $50 per month.
arkansas.link_label: Arkansas Division of Community Correction — Probation & Parole / 'On Probation' pages

california.delivery: In California, adult felony probation is run by county probation departments — each county's probation department (headed by a chief probation officer appointed under Penal Code section 1202.6) supervises people granted probation by that county's Superior Court. There is no state probation supervision agency; the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation handles parole, not probation.
california.violations: California's probation statute (Penal Code section 1203.2) provides that a probation officer or prosecutor who believes a condition was violated can ask the court to revoke probation; the court can issue a warrant, the person is brought before the court for a violation hearing with the right to counsel, and the court may continue probation on the same or modified terms, or revoke probation and impose the suspended sentence.
california.link_label: California Courts (judicial branch) — county probation structure; CA DOJ Interstate Compact page (state probation officer directory)

colorado.delivery: In Colorado, probation is part of the Judicial Branch: the Division of Probation Services in the State Court Administrator's Office oversees probation departments in each of the state's judicial districts, and district probation officers supervise people placed on probation by the courts. Private probation providers also supervise some lower-level cases under contract in some districts.
colorado.violations: The Colorado Judicial Branch's probation materials describe the process: a probation officer files a complaint or motion to revoke probation with the court, the person is entitled to a hearing before the judge, and the court can continue probation, change the conditions, extend the term, or revoke probation and impose sentence, including jail or prison time.
colorado.early: Colorado law (section 18-1.3-103.5, C.R.S.) and Judicial Branch guidance allow early termination: a person can ask the court (often through the probation officer's recommendation) to end probation early after completing a portion of the term and meeting conditions, and the court can grant early discharge from probation.

connecticut.delivery: In Connecticut, adult probation is run by the Court Support Services Division (CSSD) of the Connecticut Judicial Branch. CSSD's Office of Adult Probation offices across the state supervise people placed on probation by the Superior Court.
connecticut.violations: CSSD's official 'Probation' brochure describes the process: if a person on probation does not follow the conditions, the probation officer can return the case to court and seek a warrant for violation of probation; the person is brought before a judge for a hearing, and the judge can continue probation, add or change conditions, extend the term, or revoke probation and impose the sentence that had been suspended.
connecticut.early: Connecticut's probation statute (Conn. Gen. Stat. section 53a-29) provides that the court may terminate probation early and discharge the person once a portion of the probation period has been satisfactorily completed, and CSSD materials note that officers can recommend early termination to the court for people who have complied with all conditions.
connecticut.fees: Connecticut law (Conn. Gen. Stat. section 53a-29) requires a person sentenced to a period of probation to pay the court a one-time fee of $200. If the person first serves prison time on the case, the fee is not due until they are released and probation supervision begins. Court-ordered fines, restitution, and program costs can come on top of that.
connecticut.link_label: Connecticut Judicial Branch — Court Support Services Division (Adult Probation)

delaware.delivery: In Delaware, adult probation is supervised by the Bureau of Community Corrections, part of the Delaware Department of Correction. Its Probation and Parole officers, working from offices in each county, supervise people placed on probation by the courts using graduated supervision levels (Level I through Level III probation).
delaware.violations: Delaware DOC's Bureau of Community Corrections describes violation handling in its official policy pages: the officer files a violation report with the sentencing court, the court holds a violation-of-probation hearing, and the judge can continue probation as-is, move the person to a stricter supervision level or add conditions, or revoke probation and impose the suspended jail or prison sentence.
delaware.early: The Bureau of Community Corrections' official policy (Early Discharge from Level I-III Probation, quoted on the DOC site) says probationers on Levels I, II, and III may earn early discharge: officers review cases for compliance and can recommend to the court that probation end before the full term once the person has completed conditions and a portion of the sentence.
delaware.link_label: Delaware Department of Correction — Bureau of Community Corrections (Probation & Parole)

florida.delivery: In Florida, adult probation is supervised by the Florida Department of Corrections (FDC) through its Probation Services offices (community corrections). Correctional probation officers in circuit offices across the state supervise people placed on probation by the circuit courts.
florida.violations: Florida DOC's probation pages describe the violation process: the probation officer prepares a violation report and affidavit for the sentencing court, the court can issue a warrant for the person's arrest, and at the violation hearing the judge can revoke probation and impose the sentence, modify the conditions, or reinstate/continue probation on the same or new terms.
florida.early: Florida DOC probation materials describe early termination: a person on probation may ask the sentencing court for early termination once at least half of the probation term has been completed and all conditions have been met, and the probation officer reports the person's compliance status to the court for that decision.
florida.fees: Florida DOC publishes cost-of-supervision information: probationers must pay a monthly cost of supervision fee as ordered by the court under section 948.09, Florida Statutes, with the amount based on the statewide cost rate the department publishes.
florida.link_label: Florida Department of Corrections — Probation Services

georgia.delivery: In Georgia, adult felony probation is supervised by the Georgia Department of Community Supervision (DCS), a state agency created in 2015 that took over felony probation from the Department of Corrections. DCS community supervision officers in circuit offices supervise felony probationers (and parolees). Misdemeanor probation in Georgia is handled separately, usually by county or private probation providers overseen by the courts and the Misdemeanor Probation Oversight Unit.
georgia.violations: DCS describes the violation process on its official pages: the supervision officer can file a violation report and seek a warrant; the person gets a revocation hearing before the sentencing court, where the judge can continue probation, add or change conditions (including treatment or jail sanctions where authorized), or revoke probation and require the person to serve some or all of the remaining sentence.
georgia.early: DCS states that people on felony probation may qualify for early termination of supervision: the 'Behavioral Incentive Date'/early compliance review process lets officers recommend, and courts grant, early termination once a person has served a set portion of the sentence in full compliance (DCS publishes guidance on early termination for qualifying felony probationers).
georgia.fees: Georgia DCS states that felony probationers pay a monthly supervision fee of $23 per month, plus a one-time $50 fee in felony cases (Ga. Code section 42-8-34), on top of any court-ordered fines, restitution, and program costs.
georgia.link_label: Georgia Department of Community Supervision — Community Supervision / Probation

hawaii.delivery: Adult probation in Hawaii is run by the Adult Client Services Branch of the Hawaii State Judiciary (the courts), not the corrections department. Each circuit court's Adult Client Services section supervises people placed on probation by that circuit court and provides presentence investigation reports to the court.
hawaii.link_label: Hawaii State Judiciary — Adult Client Services (Probation)

idaho.delivery: In Idaho, adult felony probation is supervised by the Idaho Department of Correction's Division of Probation and Parole, which runs district offices across the state. Misdemeanor probation is handled separately by county misdemeanor probation departments (for example, Ada County Misdemeanor Probation).
idaho.link_label: Idaho Department of Correction — Probation and Parole

illinois.delivery: In Illinois, adult probation is run by county probation departments under the chief judge of each judicial circuit, with standards and oversight from the Administrative Office of the Illinois Courts' Probation Services Division. There is no single state probation agency delivering supervision; each county department supervises people placed on probation by its circuit court.

indiana.delivery: In Indiana, adult probation is run by county probation departments that work for the local courts, operating under standards set by the Indiana Office of Court Services and the Judicial Conference of Indiana. Probation officers supervise people sentenced to probation by the county courts and report back to those courts.
indiana.link_label: Indiana Office of Court Services — Adult Probation Standards

iowa.delivery: In Iowa, adult probation is delivered by eight judicial district departments of correctional services — community based corrections (CBC) districts — governed by local boards, while the Iowa Department of Corrections provides oversight and runs the statewide Iowa Corrections Offender Network (ICON). District probation and parole officers supervise people placed on probation by the district courts.
iowa.early: Iowa's Department of Corrections discharge-consideration policy states that a person on probation may be considered for early discharge once minimum supervision requirements have been met.
iowa.fees: Iowa law charges a person on probation a $300 enrollment fee to the supervising district department (Iowa Code section 905.14), and discharge from probation under section 907.9 is tied to those fees: once the purposes of probation are fulfilled, the court or the probation officer may order discharge when the fees are paid, or on condition that unpaid fees be paid.
iowa.link_label: Iowa Department of Corrections — Community Based Corrections / About Us

kansas.delivery: In Kansas, supervision splits by case type: court services officers who work for the district courts (under the Kansas Judicial Branch's Office of Judicial Administration) supervise most misdemeanor and lower-level probation cases ('court services'), while Kansas Department of Corrections parole services and local community corrections agencies handle higher-risk felony supervision. The sentencing court keeps authority over the probation itself.
kansas.link_label: Kansas Judicial Branch — Court Services / Kansas DOC Community Corrections

kentucky.delivery: In Kentucky, adult probation and parole supervision is run by the Kentucky Department of Corrections, Division of Probation and Parole, whose officers supervise people placed on probation by the circuit courts in districts across the state. The Division's stated mission is to supervise offenders on probation and parole using evidence-based practices.
kentucky.early: The Division of Probation and Parole's official public notices state that early termination of probation is decided by the sentencing court, and that the probation and parole officer reports to the court on whether the person has followed all orders of the court, made restitution, and otherwise been compliant. (Notices posted 05/2024.)
kentucky.link_label: Kentucky DOC — Division of Probation and Parole

louisiana.delivery: In Louisiana, adult probation and parole supervision is run by the Division of Probation and Parole inside the Department of Public Safety and Corrections (DPS&C), with district offices across the state. Its agents supervise people placed on probation by the district courts as well as parolees released from prison.
louisiana.fees: Louisiana law (Code of Criminal Procedure Art. 895.1) requires the court to order a monthly supervision fee of between $60 and $110 for supervised probation, with the exact amount set by the court; unsupervised probation carries a fee of no more than $1 per month.

maine.delivery: In Maine, adult probation is supervised by the Division of Adult Community Corrections within the Maine Department of Corrections, through regional offices. Its probation officers supervise people placed on probation by Maine courts and also manage deferred dispositions and administrative release cases.
maine.fees: Maine Department of Corrections states it collects supervision fees ordered by the court in probation cases, generally ranging from $10 to $50 per month.

maryland.delivery: In Maryland, adult probation is supervised by the Division of Parole and Probation (DPP) within the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS). DPP agents supervise people placed on probation by the District Court and Circuit Courts, and the Drinking Driver Monitor Program is also part of DPP.
maryland.early: The Division of Parole and Probation maintains an official Early Termination of Probation policy (issued June 25, 2024): a supervising agent may recommend that the court terminate probation supervision early, and DPP supervision can close once the sentencing court approves, when the person has completed all required conditions of probation.
maryland.link_label: Maryland DPSCS — Division of Parole and Probation

massachusetts.delivery: In Massachusetts, adult probation is run by the Massachusetts Probation Service, which is part of the Massachusetts Trial Court. Local probation departments in the Superior Court and District Court supervise people placed on probation by those courts.
massachusetts.violations: According to the Massachusetts Trial Court Probation Manual, a probation officer who believes there is probable cause of a violation files a Notice of Violation and a summons or warrant is issued. The court holds an initial hearing, then a final surrender hearing where the probation department must prove the violation by a preponderance of the evidence; the person has the right to be represented by an attorney, to testify, and to present witnesses. If the court finds a violation, it can terminate the probation unsuccessfully and impose sentence, keep the person on probation on the same terms, or change the terms and extend probation.

michigan.delivery: In Michigan, felony probation is supervised by the Michigan Department of Corrections (MDOC) through its local probation offices, while misdemeanor probation is supervised by probation departments run by the local courts. MDOC's probation supervision works closely with the sentencing court, including mandatory monthly reporting to the court.
michigan.violations: MDOC says the court can issue a warrant or bench warrant when a probationer is believed to have violated probation, and the probationer is brought before the court (the first hearing is usually within 14 days). This is called a Probation Violation Hearing or 'surrender'; if a violation is found, the judge can continue probation under the same or added conditions, extend the probation period, or revoke probation and sentence the person to jail or prison.

minnesota.delivery: Minnesota has three probation delivery systems, according to the Minnesota Department of Corrections: counties that joined the Community Corrections Act run their own corrections agencies, the state Department of Corrections provides probation and supervised release services in the remaining counties, and some counties use county probation officers (the CPO system) for lower-level cases. Which one supervises a person depends on the county and the case.
minnesota.violations: Minnesota's probation violation process is set by court rule and statute rather than a plain-language DOC page: the probation agent files a violation report, the court holds a hearing where the person has the right to counsel (a public defender if they qualify), and if a violation is proven the court can continue probation, add or change conditions, or revoke the stay and execute the sentence. (Summary drawn from Minn. R. Crim. P. 27.04 and Minn. Stat. § 609.14 as published by the Office of the Revisor of Statutes.)
minnesota.link_label: Minnesota Department of Corrections — Corrections agency services by county

mississippi.delivery: In Mississippi, adult probation is supervised by the Mississippi Department of Corrections (MDOC) through its Community Corrections division. MDOC probation and parole officers supervise people placed on probation by the circuit courts, including people on Earned Release Supervision and other court-ordered supervision.
mississippi.early: MDOC's official Earned Release Supervision page explains that people on ERS serve their supervision in the community under a court order and that MDOC can recommend early termination of ERS to the sentencing court once the person has completed the requirements of the program; it is a form of post-release court-ordered supervision rather than ordinary probation.
mississippi.fees: Mississippi law (Miss. Code section 47-7-49) sets the fee at $55 per month for people under MDOC field supervision, unless a hardship waiver is granted.

missouri.delivery: In Missouri, adult probation is supervised by the Board of Probation and Parole, a division of the Missouri Department of Corrections. Probation and parole officers in district offices around the state supervise people placed on probation by the courts.
missouri.violations: Missouri's Board of Probation and Parole describes the violation process on its official Violation Process and Procedures page: when an officer believes a condition was violated, a violation report (and sometimes a warrant or citation) is sent to the sentencing court, which decides whether to hold a hearing; at the hearing the court can continue probation, change conditions, or revoke probation and impose the sentence.
missouri.early: Missouri's Board of Probation and Parole says on its Earned Compliance Credits page that people on probation earn 30 days of credit for each full month they are in compliance with their conditions, and those credits can shorten the probation term; the board notifies the court when credits have reduced the term to time served.
missouri.link_label: Missouri Department of Corrections — Board of Probation and Parole

montana.delivery: In Montana, adult probation is supervised by the Probation and Parole Division of the Montana Department of Corrections. Its probation and parole officers supervise people the courts place on probation (deferred or suspended sentences) in regional offices across the state.
montana.link_label: Montana Department of Corrections — Probation and Parole Division

nebraska.delivery: In Nebraska, adult probation is administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts and Probation, part of the Nebraska Judicial Branch. Probation officers in 12 probation districts across the state supervise people placed on probation by the county and district courts.
nebraska.violations: The Nebraska Judicial Branch says a person who violates probation conditions will be arrested or issued a citation and will have a hearing before the judge; if the judge finds a violation, the judge can impose any sentence that could have been imposed for the original crime, extend the term of probation, or impose additional conditions.
nebraska.link_label: Nebraska Judicial Branch — Adult Probation Services

nevada.delivery: In Nevada, adult probation for felony and gross misdemeanor cases is supervised by the Nevada Division of Parole and Probation, part of the Department of Public Safety. County and court programs handle most misdemeanor probation separately from the state division.
nevada.early: Nevada's Division of Parole and Probation says on its official page that probation can be ended early through honorable discharge: the statute (NRS 176A.860) provides that a probationer who has completed the requirements may be granted an honorable discharge before the full term ends.
nevada.link_label: Nevada Division of Parole and Probation (DPS)

new-hampshire.delivery: In New Hampshire, adult probation is supervised by the Division of Field Services of the New Hampshire Department of Corrections. Probation and parole officers in district offices supervise people placed on probation by the courts.
new-hampshire.link_label: New Hampshire Department of Corrections — Field Services (Probation/Parole)

new-jersey.delivery: In New Jersey, adult probation is run by the Probation Division of the New Jersey Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts). Probation officers in each county's Superior Court vicinage supervise people placed on probation by the Superior Court.
new-jersey.violations: The New Jersey Judiciary says a probation officer will file a Violation of Probation (VOP) complaint when a probationer is not following the conditions of supervision; the probationer appears before a judge, and the violation must be proved by a preponderance of evidence. Possible outcomes the Judiciary lists are continuing probation as-is, extending and/or modifying the conditions of probation, or violating (revoking) the probation and resentencing the person.
new-jersey.link_label: New Jersey Courts — Probation Services (Adult Probation)

new-mexico.delivery: In New Mexico, adult probation is supervised by the Probation and Parole Division of the New Mexico Corrections Department. The Division's field offices supervise people placed on probation by the district courts, along with parolees.
new-mexico.link_label: New Mexico Corrections Department — Probation and Parole Division

new-york.delivery: In New York, adult probation is run by county probation departments (and the New York City Department of Probation), which work for the local criminal courts. The state Office of Probation and Correctional Alternatives, part of the Division of Criminal Justice Services, funds, regulates, and sets standards for those local departments but does not supervise cases itself.
new-york.early: New York's Criminal Procedure Law 410.90 (official NY Senate legislation text) allows the court to terminate probation early: it provides that the court may at any time modify or enlarge the conditions, or terminate the sentence of probation, once the person has shown satisfactory compliance during the first year or, afterward, that continued supervision is no longer necessary.
new-york.fees: One fee is set by state law: for probation cases from Vehicle and Traffic Law Article 31 offenses (such as DWI), a county that has adopted a local law may charge a probation administrative fee of $30 per month (Executive Law section 257-c), which must be waived in whole or part where paying it would work an unreasonable hardship. Other probation fees depend on the county and the case.
new-york.link_label: NY DCJS — Office of Probation and Correctional Alternatives / Probation

north-carolina.delivery: In North Carolina, adult probation is supervised by Community Supervision, a section of the state Department of Adult Correction. Probation and parole officers employed by the state supervise people placed on probation by the courts in every county.
north-carolina.early: North Carolina's Community Supervision section states that an officer and supervisor decide whether to recommend early termination of probation to the court based on the person's risk level and compliance, and that the court holds a hearing and decides whether to terminate, modify, or continue the probated sentence (N.C.G.S. 15A-1342(a) as summarized by the agency).
north-carolina.link_label: North Carolina Dept. of Adult Correction — Community Supervision

north-dakota.delivery: In North Dakota, adult probation supervision is provided by the Parole and Probation Division of the North Dakota Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation. Its field agents supervise people placed on probation by the district courts as well as parolees.
north-dakota.link_label: North Dakota DOCR — Parole and Probation

ohio.delivery: In Ohio, who supervises probation depends on the court: municipal and county courts run their own probation departments, courts of common pleas probation is handled by county probation departments or, in some counties, by the Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction's Adult Parole Authority under contract. The Adult Parole Authority also supervises parole and post-release control statewide.
ohio.link_label: Ohio Dept. of Rehabilitation and Correction — Adult Parole Authority / Community Supervision

oklahoma.delivery: In Oklahoma, adult probation supervision is handled by the Community Corrections division of the Oklahoma Department of Corrections, whose probation and parole officers supervise most people placed on probation by the district courts. Some deferred/suspended cases in certain counties are supervised by district attorney or private providers under local arrangements.
oklahoma.link_label: Oklahoma Department of Corrections — Community Corrections / Probation and Parole Services

oregon.delivery: In Oregon, adult probation (community supervision) is run by county community corrections agencies in all 36 counties, operating under intergovernmental agreements with the Oregon Department of Corrections, which provides funding, standards, and oversight. County probation and parole officers supervise people placed on probation by the circuit courts.
oregon.early: Oregon's community corrections pages describe earned discharge: people on probation can earn time off their supervision period for complying with conditions, which can end supervision early, under the state's earned-discharge program administered through the county agencies (as described by DOC and county community corrections pages referencing ORS 137.633).
oregon.link_label: Oregon Department of Corrections — Community Corrections

pennsylvania.delivery: In Pennsylvania, adult probation is run mainly by county adult probation and parole departments, which work for the county courts of common pleas. The state Pennsylvania Board of Probation and Parole supervises parolees (and some probation cases transferred to it), while the County Probation and Parole Officers' Firearm Education and Training Commission and the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency support county services; sentencing courts keep authority over probation cases.
pennsylvania.early: The Pennsylvania Board of Probation and Parole and county court materials state that only the sentencing court can end or shorten probation early, and a person on probation can ask the court (through their probation officer or an attorney) to consider early termination after showing good compliance; the Board itself cannot terminate a court's probation.
pennsylvania.link_label: Pennsylvania Board of Probation and Parole — About / County probation

rhode-island.delivery: In Rhode Island, adult probation is supervised by the Rhode Island Department of Corrections' Probation and Parole unit within its Adult Community Supervision functions; its counselors/officers supervise people placed on probation by the Superior and District Courts from offices at the courthouses.
rhode-island.link_label: Rhode Island Department of Corrections — Probation and Parole

south-carolina.delivery: In South Carolina, adult probation is supervised by the South Carolina Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services (SCDPPPS), a state agency separate from the Department of Corrections. Its agents in county offices supervise people placed on probation by the circuit courts, along with parolees and other supervised releases.
south-carolina.link_label: South Carolina Dept. of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services

south-dakota.delivery: In South Dakota, adult probation is run through Court Services, part of the South Dakota Unified Judicial System (the state court system). Court services officers in the state's judicial circuits supervise probationers for the circuit courts.
south-dakota.link_label: South Dakota Unified Judicial System — Court Services

tennessee.delivery: In Tennessee, adult probation is supervised by the Tennessee Department of Correction (TDOC) through its Community Supervision division. TDOC probation and parole officers in district offices supervise people placed on probation by the criminal courts.
tennessee.link_label: Tennessee Department of Correction — Community Supervision (Probation)

texas.delivery: In Texas, adult probation — officially called community supervision — is run day to day by local Community Supervision and Corrections Departments (CSCDs), which serve the courts of one or more counties. The Texas Department of Criminal Justice's Community Justice Assistance Division provides funding, standards, and oversight but does not supervise cases itself.
texas.early: Texas law (Code of Criminal Procedure art. 42A.701) builds in early-ending reviews: after a person has satisfactorily completed one-third of the original supervision period or two years, whichever is less, the judge may reduce or end supervision early; and at one-half of the period or two years, whichever is more, the judge must review the record and consider ending it, unless the person is behind on restitution they have the ability to pay or has not finished court-ordered treatment. Some offenses are excluded, including DWI offenses and offenses requiring sex-offender registration.
texas.link_label: Texas Dept. of Criminal Justice — Community Justice Assistance Division (CSCDs)

utah.delivery: In Utah, adult probation is supervised by Adult Probation and Parole (AP&P), a division of the Utah Department of Corrections. AP&P agents supervise people placed on probation by the courts as well as parolees, from regional offices statewide.
utah.link_label: Utah Department of Corrections — Adult Probation and Parole

vermont.delivery: In Vermont, adult probation is supervised by the Vermont Department of Corrections through its Probation and Parole field offices (Community Corrections). Officers supervise people placed on probation by the courts as well as parolees and people on other community supervision statuses.
vermont.early: Vermont DOC describes its earned time/reduction program under Act 56 (2021): people under supervision, including probationers, can earn time off their supervision for meeting case-plan goals, which can end supervision early once earned reductions cover the remaining term.
vermont.link_label: Vermont Department of Corrections — Probation and Parole

virginia.delivery: In Virginia, adult probation splits in two: state Probation and Parole Services districts run by the Virginia Department of Corrections supervise felony probationers and people with suspended sentences, while local community-based probation agencies (funded and overseen through the Department of Criminal Justice Services under the Comprehensive Community Corrections Act) supervise many misdemeanor and local cases for the courts.
virginia.link_label: Virginia Dept. of Corrections — Probation and Parole Services / DCJS Community Corrections

washington.delivery: In Washington, adult probation (community supervision) is run by the Washington State Department of Corrections, Community Corrections Division. DOC community corrections officers supervise people the courts place on supervision, and DOC also conducts violation hearings for many supervised cases.
washington.violations: Washington DOC states that when a person under supervision is alleged to have violated conditions, DOC holds a violation hearing process: the person receives notice of the alleged violations and a hearing (before a DOC hearing officer for DOC-supervised cases), where the standard is whether the violation is supported by a preponderance of the evidence; outcomes can include continuing supervision, adding conditions or sanctions, or, where the court retains jurisdiction, returning the case to the court for possible revocation (per DOC's violation process materials and RCW 9.95.120 / 9.94A.737 frameworks).
washington.link_label: Washington State Dept. of Corrections — Community Corrections

west-virginia.delivery: In West Virginia, adult probation is supervised by probation officers who work for the circuit courts under the West Virginia Judiciary (Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia), through its Probation Services. Parole, by contrast, is handled by the Division of Corrections and Rehabilitation.

wisconsin.delivery: In Wisconsin, adult probation is supervised by the Division of Community Corrections (DCC) within the Wisconsin Department of Corrections. DCC probation and parole agents in regional offices supervise people placed on probation by the circuit courts, along with parole and extended supervision cases.
wisconsin.link_label: Wisconsin Department of Corrections — Division of Community Corrections

wyoming.delivery: In Wyoming, adult probation is supervised by the Wyoming Department of Corrections through its Probation and Parole division (Field Services). Agents in field offices supervise people placed on probation by the district courts as well as parolees.
wyoming.link_label: Wyoming Department of Corrections — Probation and Parole (Field Services)
